top_choice_rationale: Targeted protein degradation (Crews, Deshaies, Handa) turns the cell's own ubiquitin-ligase machinery into a reagent through small-molecule induced proximity, reaching proteins with no active site and explaining how thalidomide-class drugs act through cereblon. The principle has been reproduced independently across ligases, targets and chemotypes, it changed what chemists and clinicians can do, and the three-name allocation and single citation are defensible. Buchwald-Hartwig amination is next for its clean attribution and maturity, nitrogenase third for solid structural work with an unsettled mechanism, and phase separation fourth because its chemical scope and attribution are less settled.
